caption: Celnet's adaptable architecture — pluggable market-data and product adapters flow into one celnet-proto contract wrapping a pinned zero-allocation hot core that prices the full catalogue (vanilla, five smile families incl. eSSVI, the 18-product exotic Instrument through American/Bermudan and correlated baskets plus an LSV booking engine), emits bit-identical surfaces across the GUI, Excel, SDK, CLI, WebSocket, FIX and Celer Trader, scales out over a Raft-replicated log and SPMC fan-out ring, and deploys three ways through reversible adapter swaps behind a conflating egress governor — with an explicit honest boundary on deploy-gated absolutes.
alt: Architecture diagram: inbound vendor and Celer feeds enter via a market-data seam into a navy Celnet core framed by the single celnet-proto contract (async edge, wait-free rings, pinned hot cores for ingest/surface, pricer/Greeks, risk, GPU/telemetry). The quant-engine band names five smile families including eSSVI and the full 18-product exotic catalogue (digitals, touches, eight barriers, var/vol swaps, Asian, forward-start/cliquet, quanto, TARF, accumulator, lookback, American/Bermudan, basket/best-of/worst-of, LSV booking model) with per-class validation; the plugin band shows Tier-0 native and Tier-2 wasmi as shipped and Tier-1 signed-.so / Tier-3 OS-sandbox as designed and deploy-gated. Bit-identical client surfaces sit on the right, a scale-out band names the Raft-replicated log, SPMC fan-out ring and cross-fleet risk fan-out, and Standalone/Hybrid/CelerIntegrated deployment modes plus an egress governor run along the bottom over a verbatim honest-boundary footnote.

caption: Celnet exposes one clean, unversioned contract served by the Celnet server and fanned out to six surfaces — gRPC, a byte-identical WebSocket JSON mirror, the Rust client SDK, the CLI, the 27-function Excel CELNET.* add-in, and the React/WebGPU GUI — carrying a unified 18-product exotic Instrument, the VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI smile-model selector, surface marking and the RiskService roll-up with limits, so the front-end uses the same APIs as any client and every value is bit-identical (Monte-Carlo products returning a price standard error) across them all.
alt: Architecture diagram showing a central coral-marked Celnet contract hub fanning out to six client surfaces (gRPC, byte-identical WebSocket mirror, Rust SDK, CLI, 27-function Excel add-in, React/WebGPU GUI), each labelled same contract and value bit-identical, with the contract carrying pricing, quote/RFQ, multiplex stream, the unified 18-product Instrument (vanilla through American/Bermudan and multi-asset basket), surface marking with the VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI smile-model selector, the market-series feed, the RiskService roll-up plus limits, and attribution identity, with a footnote that Monte-Carlo products carry a price standard error rather than machine precision.

caption: Celnet's quant and pricing methodology coverage — Garman-Kohlhagen vanilla with the full FX desk Greek set (FD- and AAD-validated), the volatility smile and arbitrage-free surface engine (Vanna-Volga, SABR, SVI, SSVI and eSSVI, with a Dupire local-vol surface and LSV booking model), and a full exotic, structured and multi-asset catalogue — barriers, digitals, touches, Asian, lookback, forward-start/cliquet, variance/volatility swaps, TARF, accumulator, quanto, American/Bermudan (PSOR free-boundary FD and Longstaff-Schwartz LSM) and Cholesky-correlated basket/best-of/worst-of — priced by complementary analytic, PDE, Monte-Carlo and survival-VV methods over a Sobol'/Brownian-bridge QMC engine. Analytic, PDE and golden classes are validated to machine precision against frozen QuantLib golden tables (vanilla, digital, barrier, double-barrier, touch, Heston); structured, MC, American, basket and LSV products carry an honest Monte-Carlo standard error and are checked against closed-form limits and ~26 parity rows vs independent oracles. Extensible via the Open Quant SDK plugin host (native Tier-0 and wasmi Tier-2).
alt: Three-column architecture diagram: Vanilla and Greeks; Smile and Surface (five smile models plus Dupire local-vol and LSV booking); and a grouped full catalogue (vanilla family, path-dependent, structured/MC, early-exercise American/Bermudan, and Cholesky multi-asset basket/rainbow) with a method legend and Monte-Carlo standard-error tags, over a band noting frozen-golden-table and ~26-parity-row validation, an honest MC-standard-error and GPU-ratio boundary footnote, and SDK extensibility.

caption: Celnet's surface pipeline turns broker ATM and risk-reversal/butterfly quotes into a versioned, arbitrage-free marked surface — market-to-smile strangle calibration, a switchable five-family smile-model selector (VV, SABR, SVI, SSVI and eSSVI), and butterfly, calendar and vertical no-arbitrage gates — which pricing, RFQ and RFS consume by pinned version, rejecting any unknown version rather than silently falling back to live.
alt: Left-to-right surface construction pipeline from broker quotes through strangle calibration, a five-family smile-model selector (VV, SABR, SVI, SSVI, eSSVI) and arbitrage gates to a versioned marked surface, with an official-versus-live registry below where pricing paths pin a surface version and unknown versions are rejected.

caption: Celnet's Open Quant SDK: one frozen trait contract and a tier-blind model registry route every model through the same calling convention — the Native (Tier-0) and WebAssembly-sandbox (Tier-2 wasmi) tiers are shipped and gated, while the signed-shared-object (Tier-1) and OS-sandbox (Tier-3 Landlock/seccomp) tiers are designed-and-seamed behind the same contract and proven at deploy — with only the core math primitives crossing a zero-ambient-authority capability boundary and a built-in butterfly no-arbitrage self-check, so desks run private-IP custom models in-engine, extending an already-complete catalogue (five smile families, the full exotic & structured set through American/Bermudan and correlated baskets, plus an LSV booking model) without forking Celnet.
alt: Architecture diagram of Celnet's tiered plugin host: a frozen Open Quant SDK contract and self-describing model registry feed a tier-blind registry that fans out to four execution tiers — Native and WebAssembly sandbox marked Built, and signed shared-object and OS-sandbox marked Designed/deploy-gated with dashed borders — with a capability boundary admitting only exp/ln/sqrt/norm_pdf/norm_cdf into the guest, a no-arbitrage self-check, and a desk band listing the full quant catalogue including five smile families (VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI), American/Bermudan early exercise, correlated multi-asset baskets, and an LSV booking model.

caption: Celnet's risk architecture spans book-shaped scenario risk — real repricing across a spot-vol shock grid, bucketed vega, cross-gamma and theta-roll horizons against versioned marked surfaces (VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI) — and a firm-wide OLAP position-fact cube where vanilla and exotic legs roll up over eight axes with convention-canonicalized netting, non-additive VaR/ES and FRTB-SA curvature, cascading limits, entitlement pruning and internal-only XVA (CVA/DVA/FVA over synthetic netting sets), with Book and Risk two zooms of one cube exposed identically to GUI, SDK and Excel.
alt: Two-band diagram: book-shaped scenario risk from the pricing hot core (vanilla, full exotic and structured catalogue incl. American, basket and LSV booking) into a spot-vol shock grid, bucketed vega, cross-gamma and theta-roll feeding a versioned marked-surface registry (VV/SABR/SVI/SSVI/eSSVI); and a firm-wide eight-dimension position-fact cube fed by a normalized fact stream of vanilla and exotic legs, with additive roll-up plus non-additive VaR/ES and FRTB-SbM curvature, pruned by entitlements and a cascading limit tree, a FRTB-SA and XVA tile (CVA/DVA/FVA, synthetic netting, internal-only), served to GUI, SDK and Excel, with a footnote that XVA is internal over synthetic netting sets and MC exposures carry a price std-error rather than machine precision.

caption: A relative latency ladder: in-core pricing is measured at nanosecond scale on the M4 dev host (vanilla ~42 ns p50, +13 Greeks ~125 ns p99, gated absolutely to the §1.2 budgets) while the network round-trip and wire framing dominate the budget, so pricing is never the bottleneck — flanked by zero-cost tail-percentile observability, regression- and instruction-count-gated benchmarks with a host-local GPU/CPU ratio up to ~53×, per-class validation (machine-precision golden for vanilla/digital/barrier/Heston, reported std-error for the MC/American/basket/LSV set), a deterministic build, and Raft-replicated SPMC scale-out. A muted footnote records the honest boundary: absolute cross-host wire SLOs and absolute NVIDIA GPU throughput are deploy-gated.
alt: Stepped latency-ladder diagram with measured nanosecond-scale in-core pricing steps far to the fast end and the network round-trip dominating, a dashed honest-boundary banner noting deploy-gated absolute wire and GPU numbers, plus a side panel of observability, benchmark (iai instruction gate and GPU/CPU ratio), per-class validation, deterministic-build and Raft/SPMC scale-out capabilities.

caption: Celnet's node-local hot substrate prices investment-bank-sized portfolios in-core, while a highest-random-weight partition map shards the book across the fleet, a full Raft-replicated log (election, conflicting-tail truncation, compaction and InstallSnapshot) gives bit-identical replay and hot-standby takeover, cross-fleet risk fans out to equal the single-node aggregate to 1e-12, and a conflating egress governor over a lock-free SPMC fan-out ring streams continuous two-way prices to many high-performance counterparties — with an explicit honest boundary that cross-host wire p99, cross-DC transport, dynamic membership and absolute wire SLOs are deploy/live-gated (in-repo proofs are loopback / localhost-multiprocess).
alt: Two-zone architecture diagram. Zone A, the node-local hot substrate, shows the async edge feeding pinned zero-allocation hot cores over wait-free SPSC rings, lock-free read-mostly state (atomic snapshot swap, seqlock top-of-book, cache-padded counters), blue-green handoff with a durable checksummed journal, many-instrument many-tenor batched repricing computing the full FX desk Greek set in one pass, a cross-platform GPU pricing backend (Metal / Vulkan / DX12 with an f64 CPU oracle and SIMD fallback, batch closed-form, path-MC, pathwise/LR Greeks and Sobol-QMC kernels reconciled f32-to-f64), and zero-cost observability. Zone B, the horizontal scale-out fabric, shows a highest-random-weight rendezvous partition map sharding the portfolio across nodes, Raft-replicated state with election, conflicting-tail truncation, compaction, InstallSnapshot and hot-standby takeover replaying bit-identically, cross-fleet risk fan-out (additive merge / non-additive re-gather, fan-out equals single-node to 1e-12), and a conflating egress governor over a lock-free SPMC broadcast ring (per-pair, exact conflation accounting received plus skipped equals produced) fanning continuous prices over the multiplex StreamSession and WebSocket mirror to many counterparties. A footnote states the honest boundary: cross-host wire p99, cross-DC transport, dynamic membership and absolute wire SLOs are deploy/live-gated, in-repo proofs are loopback / localhost-multiprocess, and the M4 Metal GPU path proves correctness plus host-local ratios only with absolute NVIDIA throughput deploy-gated.

caption: Celnet sits as the FX-options pricing system-of-record inside the Celer trade lifecycle, injecting price, the full FX Greek set and the calibrated surface into the market-data price path and option risk into the pre-trade and position path — with the pricing core covering five smile families (incl. eSSVI) and the complete 18-product exotic Instrument through American/Bermudan and correlated baskets plus an LSV booking model. The surrounding Celer estate is the designed integration map: the binding is seamed via DeployMode adapter traits (Standalone real and tested in-repo), while the live JVM Celer estate lifecycle is deploy/live-gated, not exercised in-repo.
alt: Two-swimlane diagram of the Celer trade lifecycle: a price path from venues (Fenics/Bloomberg/Refinitiv/EBS as integration targets) through FIX-in, celertech-marketdata, celertech-marketmerchant, distributor and a byte-identical WebSocket mirror to Celer Trader, and an order path from Celer Trader through celertech-orderrouting, celertech-risk, celertech-destination, celertech-clearing and celertech-positionmanager, with coral Celnet callouts injecting price/surface and option risk. Beneath sit a navy Celnet pricing-core panel naming five smile families including eSSVI and the full 18-product exotic catalogue (digitals, touches, DNT, eight barriers, window, var/vol swaps, Asian, forward-start/cliquet, quanto, TARF, accumulator, lookback, American/Bermudan via PSOR-FD and LSM, basket/best-of/worst-of via Cholesky MC, an LSV booking model and standalone Heston) validated by ~26 parity rows and frozen QuantLib golden tables with Monte-Carlo products carrying a price standard error, a book-and-risk cube, a one-contract/every-surface panel, and a three-deployment-mode seam. A dashed honest-boundary footnote states the Celer integration is designed and seamed via DeployMode adapters with the Standalone path real and tested in-repo, while the full live JVM Celer estate lifecycle is deploy/live-gated and not exercised in-repo.

caption: Celnet runs from one codebase in three deployment modes — Standalone, Hybrid and the designed CelerIntegrated estate-native binding — selected only by binding three adapter seams (market-data source, price sink, order and execution), with a conflating egress governor and a lock-free SPMC fan-out ring between the pricer and the estate distributor and the fleet sharded over a Raft-replicated log, so Celnet stays the FX-options pricing system-of-record (vanilla, five smile families incl. eSSVI, the 18-product exotic catalogue through American/Bermudan and correlated baskets, plus an LSV booking model) in every mode and migration is a reversible adapter swap — with an explicit honest boundary that the live JVM Celer-estate lifecycle is designed-and-seamed and proven at deploy, not exercised in-repo.
alt: A diagram showing the shared zero-allocation Celnet pricing core — listing the five smile families including eSSVI and the full 18-product exotic catalogue through American/Bermudan, correlated baskets and the LSV booking model — and three seam traits (market-data source, price sink, order and execution adapter) feeding three side-by-side deployment-mode columns: Standalone (self-contained feed handlers, native edge, built-in click-to-trade), Hybrid (per-seam mixed estate/native binding) and CelerIntegrated (marked as the designed estate-native binding, with the JVM distributor sidecar and price/Greeks/surface and option-risk injection). A conflating egress governor over a lock-free single-producer/multi-consumer fan-out ring routes prices to the estate distributor, the fleet shards over a Raft-replicated log with hot-standby takeover, and a coral honest-boundary footnote states the live JVM Celer-estate lifecycle is designed-and-seamed and proven at deploy rather than exercised against the live estate in-repo.

caption: One bidirectional StreamSession multiplexes many subscriptions through Subscribe, Snapshot, sequenced Update, gap-driven Resync and in-place Modify — with a Heartbeat that carries off-hot-path server observability (conflation drops, price p50/p99/p99.9, surface_version) — alongside an interleaved market-series flow (Subscribe to windowed Snapshot to sequenced Point for ATM vol, spot, risk reversal, butterfly and forward), then turns a streamed price into a confirmed fill via an unguessable line-bound keyed-MAC tradable token (the same mint used by the FIX lift) with last-look validity and idempotent, typed execution.
alt: Architecture diagram of Celnet's multiplex StreamSession showing the price subscription lifecycle with an observability-bearing heartbeat, resync and in-place modify paths, an interleaved market-series flow over the same session, and server-minted keyed-MAC tradable tokens resolving to an executed fill or a typed reject.
